# Job Chapter 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 424r–424v

---

**1** Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

**2** "Can a human being be of any use to God? Can even a wise person benefit him? **3** Does it matter to the Almighty whether you are righteous? Does he gain anything if your conduct is blameless?

**4** Is it because you are so reverent that he is punishing you? Is that why he brings you to trial?

**5** No — it is because your wickedness is enormous! Your sins are beyond counting!

**6** You demanded collateral from your own relatives for no good reason. You stripped the clothes off people who had nothing. **7** You refused water to the thirsty and withheld food from the starving.

**8** You thought the land belonged to the powerful — that only the privileged had a right to it. **9** You sent widows away with nothing. You broke the arms of orphans.

**10** That is why traps surround you on every side. That is why sudden terror overwhelms you. **11** That is why darkness has blinded you, and a flood of water has buried you.

**12** Isn't God in the highest heaven? Look how high the farthest stars are!

**13** And yet you say, 'What does God know? Can he see through those thick clouds to judge? **14** The clouds are a curtain hiding him — he cannot see us. He just strolls along the rim of the sky.'

**15** Are you going to stay on that ancient path — the road worn by wicked people? **16** They were swept away before their time, their foundations washed out by a flood.

**17** They were the ones who said to God, 'Leave us alone!' and 'What can the Almighty possibly do to us?'

**18** Yet it was God who filled their houses with good things! But the way the wicked think — I want no part of it.

**19** The righteous see their downfall and rejoice. The innocent mock them: **20** 'Look — our enemies are destroyed! Fire has consumed everything they had!'

**21** Submit to God and make peace with him. That is how good things will come your way.

**22** Accept his teaching. Store his words in your heart.

**23** If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you banish wrongdoing from your household,

**24** if you throw your gold in the dust, your finest gold among the stones of the riverbed — **25** then the Almighty himself will be your gold, your most precious silver.

**26** Then you will find your delight in the Almighty. Then you will be able to lift your face to God.

**27** When you pray, he will answer you. You will fulfill your vows with joy. **28** When you make a decision, it will succeed. Light will shine on everything you do.

**29** When people are brought low, you will say, 'Lift them up!' For God saves the humble.

**30** He will deliver even the guilty — and they will be delivered because your hands are clean."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The tragedy of Eliphaz:** This is Eliphaz's final speech, and it reveals the full bankruptcy of the friends' theology. In chapter 4, Eliphaz was gentle and indirect. In chapter 15, he was sharp but still argued from principle. Now, in chapter 22, he has been driven by his own theology to fabricate sins. Because suffering must have a cause, and because Job's suffering is extreme, Job's sins must be extreme. So Eliphaz invents them: exploitation of the poor, cruelty to widows, withholding basic necessities. The reader knows these are lies — chapter 1 told us Job was blameless. Eliphaz's theology has made him a false witness.

**The beautiful lie (vv.21-30):** The cruelest aspect of Eliphaz's speech is that his closing appeal is genuinely beautiful. "The Almighty will be your gold" (v.25) is magnificent theology. "He saves the lowly" (v.29) is true. But all of it rests on a false premise: that Job has sinned and needs to repent. The beauty of the words makes the wrongness of their application even more painful. This is the danger of true theology applied to the wrong situation.

**"What does God know?" (vv.13-14):** Eliphaz accuses Job of functional atheism — believing that God cannot see through the clouds. This is a distortion of Job's actual position. Job has never denied God's knowledge; he has questioned God's justice. Eliphaz cannot tell the difference.

*— PNEUMA*
